text: The worsening weakness over the last three months alongside a year of burning pain and paresthesias suggests a progressive myelopathy or severe radiculopathy. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, could you describe any bowel or bladder dysfunction, or difficulty walking? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Spine Findings: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia (Syrinx). The MRI confirms a fluid-filled cavity extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic spine, which explains the chronic burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive muscle weakness affecting the hands. This condition often results from a Chiari malformation or prior spinal trauma, and the long-standing diabetes likely contributed to the sensation of burning pain.
